policy: Fall 2026 launches and recently stocked catalogue gaps, not preorder or colour-only changes. Running Warehouse is the primary source for men's US size 9 measurements; NNormal's US product listing and fall launch announcement are used where Running Warehouse has no exact SKU. USD prices are listing snapshots. No wear-test ratings or exact launch day without evidence. Preserve existing IDs and links.

shoes.description: A structured road trainer combining GuideRails support, nitrogen-infused DNA LOFT v3 and RoadTack rubber. The new flat-knit tongue is a fit change worth trying with your usual socks. Running Warehouse lists a 10 mm offset and multiple widths for the Primer/Marlin/Ebon men's listing; width availability varies by colour and size. Compare against GTS 25 for heel hold and how the support feels on easy runs.

A cushioned stability trainer using HOKA's H-Frame rather than a rigid medial post. Running Warehouse measures 41/33 mm and lists an 8 mm offset. The men's Black/White listing includes standard and wide options. If you know the Arahi 8, try the new platform for heel hold and underfoot feel before treating it as a like-for-like replacement.

A fast road trainer with PWRRUN PBX PEBA foam and a redesigned nylon plate, not a carbon plate. Running Warehouse describes a 2 mm increase in stack over Speed 5 and a revised plate with no lateral wing. Compare the rocker and midfoot feel at tempo pace; the newer foam and taller stack do not establish a faster workout.

A high-stack performance trainer pairing FF TURBO² cushioning and a forefoot pod with a forked Pebax ASTROPLATE. The flexible element is not a carbon plate. At 45/37 mm in the retailer's measurements, it is a materially taller platform than the Endorphin Speed 6 despite the identical listed drop. Compare control through turns and comfort as pace changes.

A road racer with two layers of Lightstrike Pro and a carbon-infused ENERGYRIM running around the perimeter. The rim replaces the Pro 4's EnergyRods; it is neither a conventional solid carbon plate nor an unreinforced platform. The retailer records a 4 mm drop. Try it at race pace before switching from a familiar Pro 4.

A limited experimental road shoe with two fused carbon plates and NITROFOAM ELITE cushioning. Running Warehouse reports 57/49 mm with the heel on the ground; the cantilever changes geometry under load. PUMA describes it as not race legal. This is the distinct Fast-RB line, not the similarly named Fast-R Nitro Elite 2 or 3.

An unplated road trainer with nitrogen-infused NITROFOAM. Unlike the plated Deviate Nitro 4, the Pure is intended for runners who prefer a more flexible shoe across easy running and workouts. The men's US 9 listing measures 7.5 oz. Compare the two on a session that includes both easy and faster segments.

A road-to-trail variant, not a colour of Velocity Nitro 4. It pairs NITROFOAM with 3 mm PUMAGRIP ATR lugs for pavement, gravel and moderate trails. For a route dominated by steep mud, loose rock or technical hiking, compare outsole and protection with a trail-first model rather than assuming the same use.

The waterproof Cadí road-to-trail model, distinct from the standard Cadí. NNormal lists a GORE-TEX Invisible Fit ePE membrane, Vibram Megagrip outsole with 4 mm lugs and a nominal 35/29 mm stack. The listing does not publish a comparable size-specific weight. Consider this for easy trails in wet weather; try the exact upper before buying.

Nike's marathon racer combines ZoomX LT above a wider carbon Flyplate, ZoomX below it and dual forefoot Air Zoom units. Running Warehouse lists the men's Proto in stock and measures 6.7 oz and 42/34 mm. These are retailer measurements, not competition certification; runners entering regulated events should check the exact approved model and applicable rules.

differences: Compare the revised tongue and collar hold.
GTS 26 lists a 10 mm offset; the older record is historical.
comparisons.verdict: Keep a comfortable GTS 25 if its support works for you. Try GTS 26 for width, heel hold and the feel of its offset before replacing it.

differences: Arahi 9 uses a cushioned H-Frame platform and lists an 8 mm offset.
The Arahi 8 figures are historical.
comparisons.verdict: Try Arahi 9 on a familiar easy effort. It is not automatically an upgrade over a comfortable Arahi 8.

differences: H-Frame versus GuideRails support.
8 mm versus 10 mm listed offset.
comparisons.verdict: Try both for easy runs in equivalent widths. Prioritize how the support and heel-to-toe geometry feel, not a generic support ranking.

differences: The 6 adds PWRRUN PBX and revises the winged nylon plate.
comparisons.verdict: Try the revised rocker and plate at tempo pace if replacing the Speed 5; keep the existing pair if it already suits your sessions.

differences: The 2 introduces FF TURBO² cushioning and an updated Pebax ASTROPLATE.
comparisons.verdict: Check the new upper and underfoot control before switching; the original's historical numbers are not a verified upgrade baseline.

differences: 45/37 mm versus 39/31 mm measured stack.
Pebax ASTROPLATE versus nylon plate.
comparisons.verdict: Try the Sonicblast for a taller platform and the Speed for a lower one; compare at the pace and on the corners you train on most.

differences: ENERGYRIM perimeter reinforcement replaces EnergyRods.
4 mm versus 6 mm listed drop.
comparisons.verdict: Compare lower drop and fit during a race-pace workout before switching. Check actual prices; the older entry records a clearance offer.

differences: Carbon-infused perimeter rim versus wider Flyplate and forefoot Air Zoom.
4 mm versus 8 mm listed drop.
comparisons.verdict: Compare comfort and stability at goal pace in both shoes. Retail stack measurements do not establish race eligibility or which shoe is faster.

differences: Fast-RB 2 is an experimental, not race-legal model; it is not a numbered replacement for Fast-R 3.
comparisons.verdict: Do not choose the Fast-RB 2 for regulated racing. For an event, shortlist and check the approval of the exact alternative model instead.

differences: Pure is unplated; Deviate Nitro 4 is plated.
comparisons.verdict: Choose the Pure if you prefer flexibility across paces; try Deviate Nitro 4 if you specifically want a plated workout shoe.

differences: The Trail uses a 3 mm PUMAGRIP ATR outsole for mixed terrain.
Velocity Nitro 4 is a separate road model.
comparisons.verdict: Choose for the surface you run most. The Trail is designed for mixed routes; the road model makes sense if you mostly stay on pavement.

differences: Road-to-trail lugs versus a more protective trail and hiking build with forefoot rock plate.
comparisons.verdict: Try the Puma for pavement-to-gravel runs; look at the Traverse for rocky trails and hikes where underfoot protection matters more.

differences: GORE-TEX Invisible Fit and 4 mm Vibram lugs versus the Puma's 3 mm PUMAGRIP ATR outsole.
The mixed manufacturer and retailer measurement bases do not support a precise geometry or weight delta.
comparisons.verdict: Consider the Cadí GTX if a waterproof upper matters for your usual routes. Compare the Velocity Nitro Trail if your runs mix pavement and gravel.

differences: The Cadí GTX is a waterproof easy-trail model, not a numbered Tomir successor.
The Tomir record is historical.
comparisons.verdict: Compare the exact upper, outsole and surface needs. Do not substitute this for a size- or conditions-matched fit test.
